caching.title: Local Cache
caching.description: Cache responses locally with two complementary lookup paths: <1>direct</1> hash matching for exact replays, and <2>semantic</2> similarity search for related content. Send the <3>x-bf-cache-key</3> header to scope cached responses to a tenant or feature.
caching.requiresVectorStore: Requires a vector store to be configured and enabled in <1>config.json</1>.
caching.loadFailedFallback: An unexpected error occurred. Please try again.
caching.enableDescription: Loads (or unloads) the plugin without a server restart. Configuration changes you make below mutate the live plugin in place, no redeploy needed.
caching.modeSemanticDisabledTitle: Configure an embedding-capable provider to enable semantic mode.
caching.modeDirectDescription: Direct-only mode hashes each request and replays an exact match. No embeddings, no provider needed. Cheapest path, perfect for stable prompts.
caching.modeSemanticDescription: Direct + semantic mode adds vector similarity search on top of direct hash matching. Requires an embedding-capable provider and the model's real dimension. Direct hits are still served first; semantic search runs only when the direct lookup misses.
caching.headsUp: <1>Heads up:</1> a vector store namespace can only hold vectors of <2>one</2> dimension. Whenever you change the embedding <3>provider</3>, <4>model</4>, or <5>dimension</5>, make sure the <6>dimension</6> still matches what the model produces, otherwise writes to the existing namespace will fail and reads will silently miss. The namespace is <7>not</7> recreated automatically; either use a fresh namespace or drop the existing class/index in your vector store before saving.
caching.embeddingModelSearchPlaceholder: Search or type an embedding model...
caching.apiKeyInheritedNote: API keys are inherited from the embedding provider's main configuration, you don't need to add them again here.
caching.dimensionHelp: Vector size produced by the embedding model. Must match the model exactly (e.g. <1>1536</1> for OpenAI <2>text-embedding-3-small</2>, <3>3072</3> for <4>text-embedding-3-large</4>, <5>768</5> for many Cohere/Voyage models).
caching.ttlHelp: How long cached entries live before they expire. Override per-request via the <1>x-bf-cache-ttl</1> header.
caching.thresholdHelp: Minimum cosine similarity for a semantic hit. Override per-request via <1>x-bf-cache-threshold</1>.
caching.namespaceHelp: Bucket/index name where cache entries live. Leave blank to use the default (<1>BifrostLocalCachePlugin</1>). Changing this points the plugin at a different (possibly empty) bucket. Old entries are not deleted, they just stop being queried.
caching.defaultCacheKeyHelp: Fallback partition key used when a request doesn't set <1>x-bf-cache-key</1>. Cache keys isolate entries: same key ↔ shared cache pool. Leave blank to <2>disable caching</2> for any request that doesn't send the header.
caching.conversationHistoryThresholdHelp: Skip caching for conversations with more than this many messages. Long histories rarely match exactly and inflate the cache without paying off.
caching.excludeSystemPromptHelp: Strip system messages from the cache key.
caching.cacheByModelHelp: Include model name in the cache key. Different models won't share cached responses.
caching.cacheByProviderHelp: Include provider name in the cache key. Different providers won't share cached responses.
caching.overrideKey: <1>x-bf-cache-key</1>: scope this request to a specific cache partition.
caching.overrideTtl: <1>x-bf-cache-ttl</1>: override TTL for just this request.
caching.overrideType: <1>x-bf-cache-type</1>: send <2>direct</2> or <3>semantic</3> to limit lookup to one path.
caching.overrideNoStore: <1>x-bf-cache-no-store</1>: <2>true</2> to skip writing the response (still serves cached hits).

mcp.title: MCP Settings
mcp.description: Configure MCP (Model Context Protocol) agent and tool settings.
mcp.agentDepthDescription: Maximum depth for MCP agent execution.
mcp.toolTimeoutDescription: Maximum time in seconds for tool execution.
mcp.toolSyncIntervalDescription: How often to refresh tool lists from MCP servers. Set to 0 to disable.
mcp.disableAutoToolInjectDescription: When enabled, MCP tools are not automatically included in every request. Tools are only injected when explicitly specified via request headers (<1>x-bf-mcp-include-tools</1>) and still must be allowed by the virtual key MCP configuration.
mcp.tempTokenAuthDescription: When enabled, per-user MCP OAuth links can include a short-lived scoped token so someone without an active Bifrost dashboard session can complete the flow. Keep disabled to require normal dashboard authentication.
mcp.bindingLevelDescription: How tools are exposed in the VFS: server-level (all tools per server) or tool-level (individual tools).
mcp.vfsServerLevelNote: All tools per server in a single .py file
mcp.externalClientUrlDescription: Override Bifrost's public base URL when it runs behind a reverse proxy. <1>Leave blank to derive the URL</1> from the incoming <2>Host</2> header. Used as the <3>redirect_uri</3> Bifrost registers with upstream OAuth providers when it acts as a client to an MCP server (e.g. Notion or Jira redirect the browser to <4><URL>/api/oauth/callback</4> after login). Supports env var syntax (e.g. <5>env.BIFROST_EXTERNAL_URL</5>).
mcp.changeUrlWarningTitle: Changing this URL can break existing MCP clients
mcp.changeUrlWarningBody: Upstream OAuth providers lock the <1>redirect_uri</1> to whatever was registered initially, so MCP clients that already completed OAuth will fail with <2>"Invalid redirect URI"</2>. To recover, clear the stored OAuth client credentials for the affected MCP servers and re-authorize so Bifrost re-runs Dynamic Client Registration with the new URL.
mcp.authModeDescription: Controls how inbound MCP clients (e.g. Claude Code, Cursor) authenticate to the <1>/mcp</1> endpoint. <2>headers</2> (default) - VK / api-key / session headers only, OAuth discovery disabled. <3>both</3> - accepts header credentials and Bifrost-issued JWTs; existing integrations are unaffected. <4>oauth</4> - JWTs only; VK and header access is disabled.
mcp.oauthDisabledWarningTitle: VK / header MCP access will be disabled
mcp.oauthDisabledWarningBody: All existing MCP integrations that use a virtual key, api-key, or session header will stop working immediately. Clients must re-authenticate via the OAuth consent flow to obtain a JWT before they can connect.
mcp.headersDowngradeWarningBody: All MCP clients that authenticated via the OAuth consent flow will lose access; their JWTs will be rejected and their refresh tokens will become unusable. They will need to reconfigure using a virtual key or api-key header.
mcp.bothModeNote: Existing VK / header integrations continue to work unchanged. New MCP clients can connect via OAuth - they'll be redirected to the consent page to pick an identity.
mcp.issuerUrlDescription: Stable public URL advertised in discovery documents and embedded as the <1>iss</1> claim in every JWT. Leave blank to derive it from the request <2>Host</2> header (sufficient for most deployments). Multi-host or reverse-proxy deployments might need this. Supports env var syntax (e.g. <3>env.BIFROST_ISSUER_URL</3>).
mcp.authCodeTtlDescription: How long the one-time code is valid after the consent page redirects back to the MCP client (default: 300, max 900 = 15 min).
mcp.accessTokenTtlDescription: Lifetime of issued JWT Bearer tokens. Clients silently refresh when expired (default: 600 = 10 min). Also bounds how long a revoked grant keeps working before it is cut off.
mcp.requireIdpLoginDescription: When enabled, the OAuth consent flow only offers identity-provider login. Virtual keys can no longer be used to obtain an MCP token, and existing virtual-key OAuth sessions lose access immediately. Anonymous session access is unaffected (controlled by Enforce Authentication on Inference).
mcp.vkIdentityStopTitle: Virtual-key MCP access via OAuth will stop
mcp.vkIdentityStopBody: MCP clients that authenticated with a virtual key will lose access immediately and must sign in through your identity provider to reconnect.

security.title: Security Settings
security.description: Configure security and access control settings.
security.authTypeLoadError: Could not load authentication type. Dashboard password settings are hidden until this request succeeds. {{error}}
security.passwordSectionDescription: Set up authentication credentials to protect your Bifrost dashboard. Once configured, use the generated token for all admin API calls.
security.passwordHelp: Use at least 12 characters with uppercase, lowercase, number, and special character. Env var references are accepted.
security.setupTokenPlaceholder: Paste the setup token configured by your operator
security.setupTokenHelp: No admin account exists yet, so this instance is reachable without a password. To finish setup, ask your operator for the setup token configured via <1>setup_token</1> in <2>config.json</2> (or the <3>BIFROST_SETUP_TOKEN</3> environment variable) and paste it here.
security.setupTokenErrorMessage: Enter the setup token configured by your operator to create the first admin account. It's set via setup_token in config.json or the BIFROST_SETUP_TOKEN environment variable.
security.invalidOriginsToast: Invalid origins: {{origins}}. Origins must be valid URLs like https://example.com, wildcard patterns like https://*.example.com, or "*" to allow all origins
security.enforceAuthDescriptionEnterprise: Require authentication (virtual key, API key, or user token) for all inference endpoints.
security.enforceAuthDescriptionOss: Require a virtual key for all inference requests.
security.dualCredentialDescription: How to handle inference requests that present both an identity provider access token (<1>Authorization: Bearer</1>) and a virtual key (<2>x-bf-vk</2>). <3>Prefer IDP token</3> uses the user token for identity, <4>Prefer virtual key</4> drops the IDP token and authenticates via the virtual key, and <5>Reject request</5> returns a 400 error.
security.allowDirectKeysDescription: When enabled, callers can pass a provider API key directly in the <1>Authorization</1>, <2>x-api-key</2>, or <3>x-goog-api-key</3> header alongside <4>x-bf-direct-key: true</4>. Bifrost will use that key directly, bypassing the registered key pool.
security.allowedOriginsDescription: Comma-separated list of allowed origins for CORS and WebSocket connections. Localhost origins are always allowed. Each origin must be a complete URL with protocol (e.g., https://app.example.com, http://10.0.0.100:3000). Wildcards are supported for subdomains (e.g., https://*.example.com) or use "*" to allow all origins.
security.allowedHeadersDescription: Comma-separated list of allowed headers for CORS.
security.requiredHeadersDescription: Comma-separated list of headers that must be present on every request. Requests missing any of these headers will be rejected with a 400 error. Header names are case-insensitive.
security.whitelistedRoutesDescription: Comma-separated list of routes that bypass the auth middleware. Requests to these routes will not require authentication. System routes like <1>/health</1>, <2>/api/session/login</2>, and <3>/api/session/is-auth-enabled</3> are always whitelisted regardless of this setting.

clientSettings.description: Configure client behavior and request handling.
clientSettings.dropExcessRequestsDescription: If enabled, Bifrost will drop requests that exceed pool capacity.
clientSettings.droppedRequestsNote: Have dropped <1>{{count}} requests</1> since last restart.
clientSettings.disableDbPingsLabel: Disable DB Pings in Health Check
clientSettings.disableDbPingsDescription: If enabled, the /health endpoint will skip database connectivity checks and return OK immediately.
clientSettings.dumpErrorsDescription: If enabled, full error details are written to the server console logs. Useful for debugging, but may be noisy in production.
clientSettings.asyncJobTtlDescription: Default time-to-live for async job results in seconds. Results are automatically cleaned up after expiry.
clientSettings.headerForwardingDescription: Control which extra headers are forwarded to LLM providers.
clientSettings.prefixedHeadersItem: <0>Prefixed headers:</0> Use <1>x-bf-eh-*</1> prefix. For example, <2>x-bf-eh-custom-id</2> is forwarded as <3>custom-id</3>.
clientSettings.directHeadersItem: <0>Direct headers:</0> Any header explicitly added to the allowlist can be forwarded directly without the prefix (e.g., <1>anthropic-beta</1>).
clientSettings.allowlistEmptyItem: <0>Allowlist empty:</0> Only <1>x-bf-eh-*</1> prefixed headers are forwarded (default behavior)
clientSettings.allowlistConfiguredItem: <0>Allowlist configured:</0> Prefixed headers filtered by allowlist, plus any direct header in the allowlist is forwarded
clientSettings.denylistItem: <0>Denylist:</0> Headers in the denylist are always blocked from forwarding
clientSettings.wildcardsItem: <0>Wildcards:</0> Use <1>*</1> at the end of a pattern to match prefixes (e.g., <2>anthropic-*</2> matches all headers starting with <3>anthropic-</3>). Use <4>*</4> alone to match all headers.
clientSettings.importantNoPrefixItem: Allowlist/denylist entries should be the header name <0>without</0> the <1>x-bf-eh-</1> prefix
clientSettings.importantExampleItem: Example: To allow <0>x-bf-eh-custom-id</0> or direct <1>custom-id</1>, add <2>custom-id</2> to the allowlist
clientSettings.securityNoteBody: Some headers are always blocked for security reasons regardless of configuration. These headers cannot be added to the allowlist or denylist:
clientSettings.allowlistDescription: Headers to allow. Enter names without the <1>x-bf-eh-</1> prefix. Any header in this list can also be sent directly without the prefix.
clientSettings.denylistDescription: Headers to block. Enter names without the <1>x-bf-eh-</1> prefix. Applies to both prefixed and direct header forwarding.

logging.title: Logs Settings
logging.description: Configure logging settings for requests and responses.
logging.enableDescription: Enable logging of requests and responses to a SQL database. This can add 40-60mb of overhead to the system memory.
logging.logsStoreRequired: Requires logs store to be configured and enabled in config.json.
logging.disableContentLoggingDescription: When enabled, only usage metadata (latency, cost, token count, status, routing IDs, etc.) is logged. Request/response content (messages, params, tool calls, and any raw provider bytes) is dropped from log records, even when <1>store_raw_request_response</1> is on. Raw-byte send-back to callers via <2>send_back_raw_*</2> is unaffected.
logging.retainContentDescription: When enabled, requests with content logging disabled (via the global setting above or the <1>x-bf-disable-content-logging</1> header) still have their full content offloaded to object storage, but the content is never shown in logs: the database row stays metadata-only and the UI/API never fetch the payload back. Content is then only readable with direct access to the storage bucket. When disabled, content for such requests is dropped entirely (current behavior).
logging.objectStoreRequired: Requires object storage to be configured on the logs store in config.json.
logging.allowContentOverrideDescription: When enabled, individual requests can override the global content logging setting using the <1>x-bf-disable-content-logging</1> header or context key, and can opt-in to persisting raw provider bytes in logs using the <2>x-bf-store-raw-request-response</2> header. Raw-byte storage requires content logging to be on, either globally, or via <3>x-bf-disable-content-logging: false</3> on the same request. If content logging is off, raw bytes are dropped from the log record even when <4>x-bf-store-raw-request-response: true</4>. Does not control sending raw bytes back to callers; see Allow Per-Request Raw Override.
logging.allowRawOverrideDescription: When enabled, individual requests can send raw provider request/response bytes back to the caller using the <1>x-bf-send-back-raw-request</1> and <2>x-bf-send-back-raw-response</2> headers. Does not affect log storage; raw-byte persistence in logs is controlled by Allow Per-Request Content Storage Override.
logging.retentionDescription: Number of days to retain logs in the database. Minimum is 1 day. Older logs will be automatically deleted.
logging.hideDeletedVkLabel: Do Not Show Deleted VirtualKeys In Filters
logging.hideDeletedVkDescription: When enabled, deleted virtual keys are excluded from Virtual Keys filter options in Logs, Dashboard, and MCP Logs.
logging.loggingHeadersDescription: Comma-separated list of request headers to capture in log metadata. Supports exact names and wildcard patterns (e.g. <1>x-custom-*</1> captures all headers with that prefix, <2>*</2> logs all headers; note that <3>*</3> will capture sensitive headers like Authorization). Values are extracted from incoming requests and stored in the metadata field of log entries. Headers with the <4>x-bf-lh-</4> prefix are always captured automatically.
